title: Watercolor — an idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Idea washes in, connections spread
scenes.purpose: Show one idea growing outward into a connected system, built ink-first and wash-second on cold-press paper.
visuals: Cool bright-white cold-press paper with fixed tooth and soft vignette
Ink contour around the large idea shape, then a rose wash blooms inside it, followed by an inner glaze and a dry-brush lifted highlight
Ink connector lines draw outward to the upper and lower node contours, which then fill with blue and sage washes
Lines converge on the right node, whose blue wash is followed by a sage glaze that overlaps it
Serif headline and spaced caption write on left to right directly on the paper

beats.development: The idea's ink contour draws from one endpoint (0 to 0.5s). The rose wash blooms inside it with a wet pooling front (0.22 to 1.0s). The headline writes on (0.45 to 1.05s), an inner glaze layers in (0.62 to 1.12s), and a highlight is lifted with a dry brush (1.0 to 1.3s).

Two ink lines reach the upper and lower nodes (0.95 to 1.47s). Each node contour draws as its line arrives. The blue and sage washes bloom inside (1.46 to 2.03s), and the ink lines toward the right node begin.
The right node's contour closes. Its blue wash and an overlapping sage glaze settle by 2.52s, while the caption writes on (2.05 to 2.47s). The full composition then holds still and readable.

findings: Primary focus moves along the system: idea, upper and lower nodes, then right node. Eye trace runs left to right along the drawn lines.
Each wash follows its own contour, which matches the reviewed ink-first, wash-second build.
All motion is settled by 2.52s, before the 2.7s legibility deadline. The background and grain never move.
justifiedHolds: The final 0.48s hold lets both copy lines and the finished system be read together.
